title: Policy
description: How the results of each rung are judged: the quantity compared, the mode of comparison, whether the rung is gated or recorded, the limit of each metric, whether a failure of the rung blocks the later ones, and whose numerical floor may exceed a tolerance. A gated metric needs a tolerance, an independent-method rung is never gated, only a gated rung blocks later ones or has a floor, and floor limits enclose their tolerance; code checks them.

version.description: The version of the policy: an integer from 1 that rises whenever a rung, a class or a limit changes.

rungs.description: A map from rung id to how the rung is judged.

metrics.description: A map from metric name to its limits and unit.

blocksLaterRungs.description: True: two engines whose pair in this rung is FAIL or ERROR are not judged against each other in any later rung for the same case.

floor.description: The engine whose numerical floor may exceed a tolerance of this rung without failing, and the engine that decides whether an excess is that floor.

tolerance.description: The largest value a gated metric may have and pass.

attention.description: The largest value a recorded metric may have without being marked for attention.

floor.description: The floor limits of the metric: the largest value between the rung's floored engine and its arbiter, and the largest between any other engine (a witness) and the arbiter for the witness to corroborate the arbiter. A witness beyond its agreement withholds no floor unless it is nearer to the floored engine than to the arbiter.
